title: Recording with British musicians; singing in London
summary: She enjoyed the British musicians; Hue magazine's photo essay on her singing in London in 1954.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How did you feel recording with British musicians?
They were good. We had a good time. When I went over in '48 -- well, this is '54. In '54, I went over there -- I went into a club. I went into a club on Bond Street. I forget the name of the club.
Well, I can dig that out of my notes if you like --

They were just -- This was a -- wasn't a private -- This was when they began to have clubs open up, because before that, they were all private little jazz clubs, right? And I went in there and -- while I was there, you know, I was asked to do a couple of albums. I did some television over there and I did some broadcasts and I made this album.
Okay. I'll tell you what I have for 1954. It's something from the magazine, "Hue," H-u-e, which is really a photo essay (inaudible). It said you singing at the Copa Cabana in London.
Copa Cabana, was that the name of it? It might've been.
And we have pictures of you and Madam Touseaux's--
The guard at Buckingham Palace and so on.
